summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 23) in which Lawrence arrives at the Half Moon Cafe, a candlelit private restaurant run off the books by a chef named Ormund. A pretty greeter with electric blue hair asks for a reservation, and Lawrence, who has shredded his cardboard ticket and is unsure of his friend's name, is led by a sweater-wearing man to a crowded table of well-dressed people in their thirties. The passage is written in a close, observational style that mixes tension about being watched with the warmth of the gathering.
one_line: Lawrence enters the candlelit, off-the-books Half Moon Cafe, where a greeter questions him and a sweater-clad friend leads him to a crowded table.
key_facts: The door at the end of the hallway had a sheet of paper reading HALF MOON CAFE, laser-printed in its center.
The room was dim and flickering, lit by candles and draped with gathered curtains.
There were four or five small tables and a long table at the back, with wine in ice-buckets at either end.
A very pretty greeter wore a conservative suit and had her hair shaved into a half-inch brush of electric blue.
The greeter asked Lawrence, "Welcome to the Half Moon. Do you have a reservation?"
Lawrence had shredded a bit of cardboard and dropped its tatters in six different trash cans.
Lawrence did not know his friend's name when the greeter asked for it.
The man who met Lawrence wore a fantastic sweater with a tight herringbone weave and ribbing down the sleeves.
The man joked, "the world's wool farmers would starve if it wasn't for me."
The greeter was told that the man was "at our table."
The restaurant is a private kitchen owned by Ormund, who runs it off the books for friends.
The narrator says Ormund "cooks like a wizard" and can make a meal of greens and a sweet potato.
A dessert of cacao nib and avocado chili chocolate is praised by the man.
The man tells Lawrence it is nice of him to come, especially since it is his last night in the city.
The large table was crowded with men and women in their thirties dressed in draping or clinging fabrics and jewelry mixing old brass with modern plastics.
